settings.name: Nicotinamide Riboside (NR)
settings.description: The main ingredient. A form of vitamin B3 your body turns into NAD+, the molecule your cells use to make energy. NAD+ levels fall as we age.
settings.why: Nicotinamide riboside reaches NAD+ in fewer steps than other forms of vitamin B3. 300mg a day is the most the UK allows in a food supplement for adults, so MUTO uses the full amount.

settings.name: Vitamin B12 (Methylcobalamin)
settings.description: Contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism, normal immune function, normal psychological function and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.why: Methylcobalamin is a form of B12 your body can use as it is. Absorbing B12 from food tends to get harder with age, so 100mcg is well above the 2.5mcg daily reference intake.

settings.name: CoQ10
settings.description: Found in every cell, where it’s part of how your mitochondria make energy. Your body makes less CoQ10 as you get older.
settings.why: 150mg sits in the middle of the range most supplements use. CoQ10 is fat-soluble, which is why we say take MUTO with breakfast: food helps your body absorb it.

settings.name: Vitamin D3 (Vegan)
settings.description: Contributes to normal immune function, normal muscle function and the maintenance of normal bones. Most of us in the UK get too little sun from October to March.
settings.why: D3 is the form your skin makes from sunlight. 50mcg (2,000 IU) is half the UK safe upper limit of 100mcg a day. The NHS advises everyone to consider vitamin D in autumn and winter.

settings.name: TMG (Trimethylglycine)
settings.description: Also called betaine, and found naturally in beetroot. Works alongside NR, supporting the body’s natural methylation processes.
settings.why: Making and clearing NAD+ uses up methyl groups, and TMG donates them. That’s why it’s often paired with NAD+ precursors like NR.

settings.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
settings.description: Contributes to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue and to the protection of cells from oxidative stress.
settings.why: Riboflavin is part of the enzymes that release energy from food. 5mg is well above the 1.4mg daily reference intake. It’s also why your urine may look brighter yellow: that’s normal.

settings.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
settings.description: Contributes to the maintenance of normal bones. Paired with vitamin D3.
settings.why: MK-7 is the longest-lasting form of vitamin K2 in the body, so once a day is enough. Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium, and K2 works alongside it.

settings.name: Zinc (Bisglycinate)
settings.description: Contributes to normal immune function, normal cognitive function and the protection of cells from oxidative stress.
settings.why: Zinc bisglycinate is zinc bound to glycine, an amino acid, a form that is well absorbed and gentle on the stomach. 15mg is 150% of the daily reference intake and within the UK safe level of 25mg a day. It’s paired with copper, because taking zinc long-term can lower copper levels.

settings.name: Folate (5-MTHF)
settings.description: Contributes to normal immune function, normal psychological function and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.why: 5-MTHF is the active form of folate. Many people carry a common gene variant (MTHFR) that makes converting ordinary folic acid less efficient, so we skip that step. 400mcg is 200% of the daily reference intake.

settings.name: PQQ
settings.description: Pyrroloquinoline quinone. Found in small amounts in foods like kiwi, parsley and green tea, and studied for its role in the mitochondria, where cells make energy.
settings.why: 20mg a day is the amount most often used in human studies of PQQ.

settings.name: Trans-Resveratrol
settings.description: A plant compound found in grape skins, widely studied in healthy-ageing research.
settings.why: Trans-resveratrol is the stable, active form of resveratrol. It’s fat-soluble, so it’s best taken with food, like the rest of MUTO.

settings.name: Grape Seed Extract
settings.description: Plant polyphenols from grape seeds. Paired with trans-resveratrol.
settings.why: Standardised to 95% polyphenols, so every batch has the same amount: about 142mg of polyphenols per serve.

settings.name: Vitamin B6 (P5P)
settings.description: Contributes to normal psychological function, normal immune function, the regulation of hormonal activity and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.why: P5P (pyridoxal-5-phosphate) is the active form of B6, ready to use. 5mg is half the UK safe upper level of 10mg a day.

settings.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
settings.description: Contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism and normal psychological function.
settings.why: 5mg is well above the 1.1mg daily reference intake. Thiamine dissolves in water and your body stores very little, so a daily dose keeps levels steady.

settings.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
settings.description: Contributes to normal psychological function and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.why: 16mg niacin equivalents is 100% of the daily reference intake. It’s on top of the NR, which is also a form of vitamin B3.

settings.name: Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
settings.description: Contributes to normal mental performance and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.
settings.why: 10mg is about 167% of the 6mg daily reference intake.

settings.name: Biotin
settings.description: Contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism and normal psychological function.
settings.why: 300mcg is six times the 50mcg daily reference intake and well within safe levels. Biotin can affect some blood test results, so tell your doctor you take it before a blood test.

settings.name: Copper (Bisglycinate)
settings.description: Contributes to normal immune function and normal energy-yielding metabolism.
settings.why: Copper bisglycinate is bound to glycine, like the zinc, so it’s well absorbed. 1mg is 100% of the daily reference intake. It’s there to keep the 15mg of zinc in balance, since zinc taken long-term can lower copper levels.

settings.name: BioPerine® (Black Pepper)
settings.description: Black pepper extract. Added to help your body take in the other ingredients.
settings.why: BioPerine is a branded black pepper extract standardised for piperine. Only a small amount is needed, and it adds no taste or heat to the capsules.
